text:
alan: quick favor — can someone run a short baseline for continuous-batching (cb) tuning on a prod-like rig? want p50/p95/p99 + throughput for small-window workloads (avg seq 512, p95 1024). compare max_batch_tokens=2048 vs 4096. 5m run per config is fine. no need to hit all regions. ping with short logs/summary when done. thx :pray:

jess: I can kick off one in us-west. which model/quantization?

alan: gpt-medium-quant please. set batcher.max_tokens=4096 and 2048. keep concurrency=8. example loadgen: `./loadgen --model gpt-medium-quant --seq-avg 512 --seq-p95 1024 --concurrency 8 --duration 300 --max-batch-tokens 4096`

sam: started the 4096 run now (job id cb-3123). will post p50/p95/p99 + tok/s every minute. ETA ~6m.

jess: started the 2048 run in us-east (job cb-3124).

runtime-bot: cb-3123: run started on node rwn-gpu-12. cb-3124: run started on node rwn-gpu-21.

maria: quick config note — please set `queue.preempt_deadline_ms=100` so we capture preemption fallback behavior. otherwise tiny bursts will skew tail latency.

alan: good call — set that. also enable `kv_cache=true`.

sam: first-minute summary (4096): throughput 480 tok/s, p50 120ms, p95 380ms, p99 920ms, tail errors 0. snippet:
```
{"minute":1, "tok_s":480, "p50_ms":120, "p95_ms":380, "p99_ms":920}
```

sam: minute-2: throughput 500 tok/s, p99 890ms, mem stable.

jess: 2048 first-minute: throughput 610 tok/s, p50 95ms, p95 260ms, p99 610ms. looks healthier under bursty arrival.

kai: quick FYI — PR#4212 changed batch.window_ms from 8 -> 4ms in staging. could affect numbers if that landed on these nodes. did it? :thinking_face:

alan: PR is in staging only, not prod nodes. runtime-bot showed rwn-gpu-12/21 which are prod-config, so these runs are unaffected.

kai: can we add one extra run with `batch.window_ms=6` (middle ground)?

jess: I can queue that after the 2048 finishes.

sam: final 4096 numbers: throughput 515 tok/s, p99 870ms, tail spikes up to 1.1s for ~0.3% of requests. full CSV uploaded: /shared/bench/cb/3123456789/4096.csv :file_folder:

jess: final 2048 numbers: throughput 630 tok/s, p99 600ms, tail >1s ~0.05%. CSV: /shared/bench/cb/3123456789/2048.csv

alan: thanks everyone. quick takeaways — for seq~512 workloads: 2048 gives better latency and slightly higher throughput; 4096 can edge throughput in some windows but increases tail. recommendation: prefer 2048 for customer-facing low-tail workloads.

maria: note for follow-up — try `adaptive-window=true` with cap 8ms to reduce tail without sacrificing batch depth. can we schedule a small sweep next week?

alan: will open an RFC and schedule. pinging @eng-runtime for reviewers. @kai can you review PR#4212?

kai: on it, will review today. :thumbsup:
